chapter: Bill Robinson and Chuck and Chuckles
title: Robinson's tour with Don Redmond's show
summary: Green introduces the story: Robinson in Shirley Temple films, then a personal appearance tour with Don Redmond's orchestra, Peg Leg Bates and Chuck and Chuckles at Boston's RKO Palace.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Tell me about the story you told me.

Well, once upon a time, as time came on or came by or passed, he eventually got into moving pictures with Shirley Temple, the child actress star. He used to teach her. He used to do choreography for him and her. And he called it terpsichore, he said, and he would make up these dance routines, tap dances, you know, like the adult and the child tap dances, and Shirley Temple and Bill Bojangles Robinson. Like they did the melody, "Bojangles of Harlem", and that went, (Singing), "Old Bojangles of Harlem," they were saving a plantation while they sang and tap danced, that they introduced in this movie. I think it was the "Little Colonel", I think it was called. Eventually he came on what you call a personal appearance tour at the time, and Chuck and Chuckles was with the Don Redmond Orchestra and show, and that was Mr. Glen Peg Leg Bates and Dan Jenkins, Chuck and Chuckles, Louise McCarroll, Sonny Woods, and starring Bill Bojangles Robinson, the World's Chamption Tap Dancer. We were in Boston, Massachusetts, at the RKO Palace, and it was during the week of his birthday. Now, as it had been quite some years since I had saw Mr. Bojangles, Bill Bojangles Robinson, see, but I had got into -- I knew him from the Rhythm Club.
